citations.title: Synchronous bronchioloalveolar and squamous cell lung cancer with different 18F-FDG avidity on PET/CT.
contexts: The value of (18)F-FDG PET/CT for the detection of synchronous extrathoracic primaries has been previously demonstrated.(5,6) Although PET/CT has been extensively used in the diagnosis and staging of lung cancer, this is the first report on PET/CT in MPLC with both true-positive and false-negative findings concerning the primaries.

citations.title: Three synchronous primary malignancies detected by F-18 FDG PET/CT: breast, rectal, and urothelial bladder carcinomas.
contexts: PET/CT can also detect 2 synchronous malignancies in different organs, which is most commonly reported in patients being evaluated for esophageal(5,6) and head and neck primary malignancies, and less commonly for lung cancer.(11,12) Sometimes, the second synchronous malignancy can only be identified as a “discordant” result after chemotherapy, and this has been reported to occur with lymphomas.

semantic_scholar.tldr: A 65-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history who was examined by his local physician for incidental right-sided chest wall pain was found to have a non-small-cell lung carcinoma, which histologic analysis showed to be poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma.
